children.title: Criteria for Research Abandonment in Automated Inquiry

detail.title: Criteria for Research Abandonment in Automated Inquiry
detail.summary: This notebook explores when research inquiries necessitate abandonment or discontinuation, identifying technical integrity risks and failing rigorous validation as two primary criteria. It distinguishes between external environment changes (e.g., concept drift) and internal reasoning flaws (e.g., unreproducible results) as objective grounds for stopping a line of inquiry.
detail.reason: This notebook synthesizes initial research on discontinuation criteria, utilizing evidence from machine learning integrity and computational biology validation failures.

detail.title: Metacognitive Monitoring for Unrecognized Reasoning Limits
detail.summary: Reasoning limits are implicitly defined by the operational boundaries of the collector and the stability of the input environment. Beyond architectural limitations, concept drift in data sources poses an unrecognized risk where agents reason on obsolete premises without internal signal of the shift.
detail.reason: Synthesizing new evidence on data drift with previous findings on architectural collector limits.

detail.title: Data-Driven Identification of Novel Research Domains
detail.summary: Automated data science practices provide a structured mechanism for identifying research problems by synthesizing large-scale domain data. When applied to fields such as carbon-capturing technology, this approach successfully isolates alternative processes as novel research targets. This framework reduces reliance on heuristic problem identification, shifting the burden to systematic analysis.
